subject: psychiatry
title: Alcohol use disorder

steps.tx: **Alcohol use disorder** ranges from hazardous drinking to dependence with craving, lost control, tolerance and continued use despite clear harm at home or work. Morning relief drinking and withdrawal tremor with sweating and fast pulse reveal physical dependence at the bedside. **AUDIT screening** quantifies risk better than the four CAGE questions about cutting down, annoyance, guilt and eye openers. Dependence still matters when drinking continues after pancreatitis, liver injury or family breakdown has already occurred repeatedly.
steps.say: Alcohol dependence brings craving and control slips away while tolerance keeps rising steadily. Morning drinking relieves tremor and sweating reveals physical dependence at assessment clearly. AUDIT is a tool that quantifies risk better and CAGE gives only a crude bedside screen for comparison. Continued drinking despite harm confirms the disorder even when liver tests look normal.

steps.tx: The timeline separates **withdrawal seizures** at 24 to 48 hours from alcoholic hallucinosis with clear consciousness and from later delirium tremens with fever and confusion. Tremor with autonomic overactivity starts within hours, hallucinosis brings auditory voices around one to two days, and **delirium tremens** arrives at 48 to 96 hours with visual hallucinations. A reducing benzodiazepine regimen with fluids and electrolyte correction treats withdrawal safely in hospital. Missing that late window costs lives, because untreated delirium tremens still kills patients.
steps.say: Withdrawal begins with tremor within hours and seizures follow at one to two days. Hallucinosis is a clear state with voices and the patient is awake while families report that change. Delirium tremens is a late state with fever and confusion and visual hallucinations are prominent during that phase. Benzodiazepine reduction helps withdrawal and fluid replacement helps correct dehydration during hospital care.

steps.tx: **Wernicke encephalopathy** from thiamine deficiency causes confusion with ataxia and ophthalmoplegia or nystagmus, although the full triad appears in only a minority of real patients. Any confused malnourished drinker therefore receives parenteral thiamine before glucose, because glucose without thiamine can precipitate the syndrome. Untreated disease progresses to **Korsakoff syndrome** with irreversible failure to form new memories and confabulation filling the gaps. Early parenteral replacement protects the brain, and oral thiamine follows once risk settles.
steps.say: Wernicke disease causes confusion and the gait becomes ataxic while eye movements fail. Most patients lack the full triad and waiting for it delays treatment dangerously. Parenteral thiamine comes before glucose because glucose alone can precipitate the syndrome quickly. Korsakoff syndrome follows untreated disease and new memories fail to form.

steps.tx: The brain view labels the thalamus, mammillary body and periaqueductal grey beside icons for confusion, ataxia and ophthalmoplegia in **Wernicke encephalopathy**. Those deep structures suffer first when thiamine runs out, which explains why eye signs and gait failure accompany the confusion. The infusion bags stress **thiamine before glucose**, because glucose alone can precipitate the syndrome in a depleted drinker. For the exam, you should give parenteral thiamine early rather than wait for the full triad.
steps.say: The diagram is useful because it shows deep brain structures and mammillary bodies are at risk when thiamine disappears completely. Confusion appears with ataxia and eye movement failure completes the classic teaching triad. Thiamine infusion comes before glucose and that order protects the depleted brain well. Examiners reward early parenteral treatment even when the triad remains incomplete.

steps.tx: **Acamprosate** supports abstinence after detoxification, naltrexone reduces heavy drinking days, and disulfiram deters drinking only in motivated patients who consent to supervised aversive treatment. Motivational interviewing, mutual aid and relapse prevention therapy strengthen every drug plan and address triggers in daily life. **Relapse prevention** also needs liver and pancreas screening, cancer awareness and reassessment of depression after abstinence settles the picture. The table below lists withdrawal timing, and examiners ask those hours repeatedly in single best answer questions.
steps.say: Acamprosate supports abstinence and naltrexone reduces heavy drinking days after detoxification finishes. Disulfiram deters drinking only when motivated patients consent and supervision keeps treatment safe. Therapy strengthens every drug plan and triggers need rehearsal before discharge home. Depression is common after abstinence and reassessment is necessary because alcohol itself can depress mood in many patients.
